verses.1: I say then, did the God not leave his people alone? No, he did not do so. For I am a Israelite, born of Abraham’s seed, from the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.2: The God did not abandon the people he had created. Or perhaps you don’t know what the scriptures say about this in the Book of Elisha. What does it mean that God acts according to Israel’s will?
verses.3: Lord, your prophets have been rejected; your sacrifices have been destroyed. I am left alone, and my soul is in need of salvation.
verses.4: But what does capitalism say to him? I forgot that there were six thousand men who didn’t get their due from Baal.
verses.5: Thus, in this present time too, a “leimma” has been created by divine choice.
verses.6: But if it’s a gift, then it’s no longer something that can be obtained through effort. For a gift doesn’t become something that can be achieved through effort at all.
verses.7: So what? What Israel demanded did not happen; however, the election did take place. The rest of them were rejected.
verses.8: As it is written: “The God gave them the spirit of blindness, and the inability to see and hear, until today.”
verses.9: And David said, “Let their tables be turned into a tomb, and let them be used as a place for burning incense and offering sacrifices.”
verses.10: Their eyes became blind, unable to see anything; their necks also became completely stiff.
verses.11: I say then, they did not fall because of their own actions. No, it was their own fault that led to their salvation for the nations, so that they could be saved.
verses.12: And if their profits are vast, and their losses also involve significant amounts of wealth for other nations, then how much more so will be their profits.
verses.13: But I say this to the nations. As for me, since I am a messenger of the nations, I glorify my ministry.
verses.14: Perhaps I can save some of their flesh and thus save some of them.
verses.15: For if their expulsion is a blessing for the world, then what kind of recruitment is it, if it isn’t a way to bring people back from death?
verses.16: And if the beginning is holy, and also the root; and if the branches are holy, too.
verses.17: If some of the branches have broken off, then you, being like a wild fire, remain united among them. You become part of the root of that growth and prosperity.
verses.18: I do not acknowledge those branches. If I were to acknowledge them, then it’s not you who will be shaken, but the branch itself.
verses.19: So, you’re asking questions. The branches have been separated so that I can be centered.
verses.20: Well then, they were led astray by their lack of faith; but you, on the other hand, remained faithful. Do not be too proud, but rather, be fearful.
verses.21: For if the God of nature’s branches did not exist, then neither will you exist.
verses.22: See therefore the usefulness and benefit of God’s actions. For those who fall, He acts with destruction; but for you, He acts with usefulness. If you follow this usefulness, then you too will be able to make progress.
verses.23: And those who do not trust him will surely be discouraged. For it is possible for God to discourage them once again.
verses.24: For if you are, by nature, a wild and untamed animal, yet by nature also you can be turned into a fine oil. Then how much more will those who are naturally wild be able to be transformed into fine oils.
verses.25: For I do not want you to know this secret, brothers, so that you may not become foolish. For from time to time, a portion of Israel has been chosen, until the full number of the nations was completed.
verses.26: And in this way, Israel will be saved. As it is written: “He who comes from Zion will bring away the sins of Jacob.”
verses.27: And this is the promise I give you, when I forgive your sins.
verses.28: In the matter of the gospel, they are your enemies; but in terms of election, they are beloved by their fathers.
verses.29: For the gifts are given back, and the glory of God is also restored.
verses.30: For just as you were once subjected to the God’s punishment, so now you have been subjected to this punishment.
verses.31: In the same way, they too have now been condemned by that same judge, so that they too may be judged.
verses.32: For the God sealed all things into a state of punishment, so that He might forgive them all.
verses.33: Oh, depth of wealth, wisdom, and knowledge about God! How unpredictable are His judgments, and how uncertain are His paths.
verses.34: Who then knew the thoughts of the Lord? Or who became his advisor?
verses.35: Who gave it to him, and who will give it back to him?
verses.36: For through him and in him, all things exist. To him belongs glory throughout all ages, indeed.
